title: A second medication added for a different condition
description: Mum takes Tablet A for her blood pressure. Later the GP also prescribes Tablet D for her thyroid, in very similar words. Nothing is replaced: both prescriptions are current, so a brain that treats the second note as a change to the first has lost the first dose.

notes.text: GP prescribed Mum 1 x Tablet A a day for her blood pressure, with breakfast.
Collected Mum's prescription from the pharmacy on Station Road.
Mum's blood pressure check is booked at the surgery on 2 March at 10:30.
Joan next door collects Mum's shopping on Thursdays.
GP also prescribed Mum 1 x Tablet D a day for her thyroid, with lunch.
Took Mum to the garden centre. She chose two pots of lavender.
Mum's reading glasses are in the blue case on the hall table.
Boiler service done. The engineer says it is fine for another year.
Mum's blood pressure check went well. Nothing for the GP to follow up.
Rita rang. She and Mum are going for lunch on Sunday.

questions.why: Both prescriptions are current. A brain that replaced the first with the second would lose Tablet A.

questions.ask: What does Mum take for her blood pressure?
questions.why: The second prescription is for a different condition and must not delete the first.

questions.ask: What does Mum take for her thyroid?
questions.why: The new prescription itself must be found.

questions.ask: What time does the swimming club start?
questions.why: Nothing in the notes mentions swimming.
